verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev is a code-first platform: tasks are plain TypeScript async functions built with a documented SDK. It also ships an official CLI, a management API with TriggerClient and API-key auth, and build extensions for customizing the bundle and container image, so developers can write private integrations directly in code. Community users corroborate this, describing it as moving workflows from n8n's GUI into the IDE and as easily integrating with their own tools. Missing for 10: no dedicated documentation for a connector or integration-building framework (custom integrations are implied through tasks rather than a first-class connector model), and no published OpenAPI spec (the probe found 404s).
